candidates.problem: Acquiring locks in transfer direction introduces a deadlock for opposing transfers.
candidates.reason: Previously, both account locks were acquired in account-number order regardless of transfer direction. Now move(A, B, amount) acquires A first, while move(B, A, amount) acquires B first. If each call acquires its source lock before either acquires its target lock, both wait indefinitely for the other's lock. The insufficient-funds guard does not prevent this when both sources have sufficient balances. Preserve the common lock ordering while performing the balance check under the locks.
